items.title: GitHub Enterprise support: per-host API endpoints for GHE.com (data residency) and self-hosted GHES
items.note: Split from C01/#623 (2026-11-01). The owner asked whether an employer's GitHub org would work. github.com orgs already do. GHE.com tenants (<tenant>.ghe.com, API at api.<tenant>.ghe.com) and self-hosted GHES (custom host, API at https://<host>/api/v3 and /api/graphql) do not: the GitHub adapter ignores SCMRepo.Host and always talks to github.com with one token, so accepting those hosts would fetch github.com/<owner>/<repo>#N. That is wrong data, so #623 keeps rejecting them. Also check what *.ghe.io links do today; they are probably mis-routed the same way. Fix: the adapter picks its API base from Repo.Host, uses a per-host token (gh auth for that host), then IsGitHubHost accepts *.ghe.com and the project's own GHES host.
items.doneWhen: A claimed PR on <tenant>.ghe.com or a self-hosted GHES host fetches that host's PR data, with tests against a fake per-host server

answers.question: How should Tallpine learn which self-hosted hosts are GitHub Enterprise Server (a GHES name like git.acme.corp looks the same as self-managed GitLab, which is today's fallback)?
answers.answer: Daemon env TALLPINE_GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_HOSTS (comma list, like TALLPINE_GITLAB_ALLOWED_HOSTS); MDM/launchd can set it

answers.question: *.ghe.io is accepted as a GitHub host today but its PRs are fetched from api.github.com (wrong data). No current GitHub product uses ghe.io (GHE.com tenants are *.ghe.com). What should happen to *.ghe.io?
answers.answer: Drop it from the built-in rules (SCM, PR URLs, tracker); a real ghe.io host can be listed as a GHES host

items.decisions:
| # | Question / assumption | Final answer | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| q1 | How GHES hosts are known | Daemon env `TALLPINE_GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_HOSTS` (comma list, entries may include `:port`), parsed like `TALLPINE_GITLAB_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | Owner answer |
| q2 | `*.ghe.io` | Dropped from every built-in rule (SCM host, PR URL, tracker inference, tracker intake parse). A real ghe.io host can be listed in q1's env | Owner answer |
| a1 | GHE.com | `*.ghe.com` built in. REST `https://api.<tenant>.ghe.com`, GraphQL `https://api.<tenant>.ghe.com/graphql`. `api.*` never a PR URL host | Accepted |
| a2 | GHES endpoints | `https://<host>/api/v3`, `https://<host>/api/graphql`; https only; listed host matched exactly, case-insensitive, port included | Accepted |
| a3 | Per-host token | `TALLPINE_GITHUB_HOST_TOKENS` (host=token,...) else `gh auth token --hostname <host>`. github.com tokens (env, account tokens) never sent to another host | Accepted |
| a4 | Missing token / unlisted host | Only that host's PRs fail (Fetched=false, auth error logged once per host); github.com/GitLab unaffected. Unlisted host rejected before any request | Accepted |
| a5 | Accounts | Multi-account auto-pick and project githubUser apply to github.com only | Accepted |
| a6 | Routing coverage | Every GitHub adapter call routes by repo host; batch GraphQL groups by (host, account) | Accepted |
| a7 | Identity | Per host via `AuthenticatedIdentityForHost` | Accepted |
| a8 | URL acceptance | claim-pr, report --pr-created/--pr-reviewed, review gateway, PR summaries accept enterprise PR URLs via the shared domain rule; CLI registers hosts from the same env (sessions inherit daemon env) | Accepted |
| a9 | Tracker intake on GHE | Out of scope; tracker stays github.com-only | Accepted |
| a10 | Git credential helper for GHES remote | Out of scope, follow-up risk | Accepted |
| a11 | Surface / split | Env only, documented beside GitLab vars; one PR | Accepted |
| n1 | How the pure domain rule learns listed hosts | Process-wide registry in `domain` set once at startup (daemon after `config.Load`, CLI root from env); empty by default | New, not confirmed by owner |
| n2 | PR URL ports | github.com/ghe.com PR URLs still reject ports; a listed GHES host with `:port` accepts that exact port | New, not confirmed by owner |
| n3 | Stored `*.ghe.io` rows | No migration; they stop being observed (they never had correct data) | New, not confirmed by owner |

items.title: Report tiering: low-value auto reports stop waking orchestrators
items.note: B117 study (artifacts/agent-orchestrator-488/b117-lane-optimizations.md): 177/260 (68%) orchestrator turns today were 'Worker reports' batches, each a full turn at 200-380k context.
items.doneWhen: Non-actionable auto items (turn_ended, checkpoint, turn_resumed, and review_approved when it needs no action) don't wake an idle orchestrator on their own: they ride along with the next real batch or coalesce over a window (e.g. 10 min); actionable items (needs_input, stuck, done, blocked, human messages) still wake immediately; measured before/after: share of orchestrator turns that are report-only

items.title: session ls has no name/label column; orchestrator missed a live worker and spawned a duplicate
items.note: 2026-11-01: grepping session ls for 'B262' found nothing, because names aren't printed, so I spawned a second B262 worker (588) while 587 was already running it. Also: spawn --backlog of a blocked item printed 'warning: B262 is blocked by B261' as the LAST line, after the 'spawned session' line, so tail -1 hid the success. Fix: add a NAME column (truncated) to session ls; print warnings before the result line; spawn --backlog refuses when a live worker already holds that item (or says so loudly).

items.title: Orchestrator lanes: several orchestrator chats per project, one topic each, with a daemon-owned merge queue
items.note: Owner (2026-10-28): wants separate chats per topic (brand/repo name, mobile app, features, deps, security) without mixing topics or drowning one orchestrator in worker reports; asked about multiple orchestrators that coordinate merges. Design: an orchestrator chat is bound to a lane = a backlog parent/topic; workers it spawns inherit the lane; reports route to the lane's orchestrator only. Coordination through shared state, not LLM-to-LLM chat: (1) backlog item/lane ownership; (2) PR area claims (paths touched) visible to all lanes with conflict warnings; (3) a daemon-owned merge queue: approved PRs are rebased, CI-gated (local CI), merged serially, with same-area ordering; (4) a short cross-lane digest (what merged, what is in flight) injected into each orchestrator on request. Size: M (2-4 PRs). Depends on B85 steering/notifications.

items.title: Account pool: spread sessions across several accounts per harness and fail over on usage limits (harness-agnostic, off by default)
items.note:
Owner 2026-10-29: for other people (not own use); "3 Claude accounts, subagents start on a random account or move when one hits limits"; must cover Codex; ideally harness-agnostic.
HAVE TODAY: multiple signed-in accounts per harness for Claude Code and Codex (backend/internal/adapters/agentaccount/claude.go, codex.go; stores agent_account_store.go, codex_account_management_store.go); per-session account binding + default account + "Use for all sessions"; durable live move of a running session to another account that resumes the same conversation (session_manager/agent_account.go:12-26 StartAccountTransition, preflight checks first); per-account rate-limit reading (agentaccount/claude.go:184-253) and usage-limit auto-resume at reset (service/chat/usage_limit.go, controller_send.go:227).
MISSING: (1) placement policy at spawn: default | random | most headroom | least used, over the harness's usable accounts; (2) auto-failover: on a usage-limit stop, pick an account with headroom and run StartAccountTransition instead of waiting for reset (cooldown, no ping-pong, fall back to wait-for-reset when all are limited); (3) harness-agnostic AccountPool interface (List/Usable/Limits/Bind) over agentaccount adapters, so Kiro/DeepSeek (API keys) can join later; (4) settings UI + MDM/managed-config keys, OFF by default; (5) B19 polish items that matter for multi-account (misdirected CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR check, ExitAgentsOnAccount move callback).
ESTIMATE: 3-4 PRs behind a switch: AccountPool+placement; failover; UI+policy keys; B19 subset. Opus first reviews (concurrency in the move path).
CAVEAT: rotating several personal Claude/ChatGPT subscriptions to get around usage limits may conflict with provider terms; frame and document it for team/org seats and API keys, and say so in the docs.

items.title: Session retention policy (auto-cleanup), user + MDM configurable
Mobile: HTTPS-only phone connection (pinned LAN cert + Tailscale Serve), drop plain http
items.note: Owner 2026-10-30: 'can't we enforce https?' Today the LAN gateway (:65221) is plain http, and TLS on the phone is a manual toggle that fails unless secure pairing (tailscale serve) is on AND the tailnet has HTTPS Certificates enabled (CertDomains was empty). Design: (1) the daemon generates a self-signed cert and the QR carries its SHA-256 fingerprint; the phone pins it, so LAN uses https with no CA; (2) tailnet uses Tailscale Serve with a real *.ts.net cert when available, otherwise the pinned cert over the MagicDNS name; (3) remove the TLS toggle from the phone and stop plain http after a migration window; existing pairings re-pair once. iOS: pinning needs a native module or a URLSession delegate (Expo config plugin). After #457 and the review follow-ups (same area).
